Sam Lott The number of charging facilities and their placement within the AMD service network, sizing of the power level for each charging station (i.e., vehicle charging position), and type of charger equipment (automated electrical contact system, wireless inductive power transfer, or conventional plug-in configuration) are fundamental parameters for any charging strategy for any given AV fleet. Another aspect of the charging strategy is the charge rate for each EV battery considering the nonlinear charging characteristics discussed previously. 46 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. A charging strategy may comprise both deep charging, typically overnight to fully replenish an EV battery pack prior to operations the following day, and short periods of “opportunity charging” during the day to extend the operational duty cycle of the vehicle. Opportunity charging is particularly relevant for on-demand vehicle fleets because of the complexity of their operations. Opportunity charging occurs during brief periods when an individual vehicle is dormant, such as at station stops. This can be momentary, corresponding to the few minutes to allow for boarding and alighting, or extended, when vehicles are pre-positioned at a station in anticipation of a surge in ridership demand. Deep charging of individual vehicles requires an extended period during which they are removed from passenger service, typically overnight. The charging strategy is fundamental to determining the available duty cycle of a vehicle, which in turn will determine the minimum size of the fleet required to meet passenger demand as well as the charging infrastructure and energy needs required. Additional opportunity charging may be afforded by the advent of wireless inductive charging technologies. Wireless inductive charging is typically a system using a pad installed in the roadbed or on the road surface to transmit electric charge to a vehicle above the pad, requiring no physical connection or human action to initiate. Although not yet mature, this technology may enable BEVs to receive additional electric charge while stopped briefly at a PUDO zone, an intersection, or other locations at which a vehicle may dwell for a short time. Wireless inductive charging may enable BEVs to operate for longer periods between deep charging cycles or even indefinitely.
